description: The 3D bar chart illustrates the accuracy of three large language models—Davinci-003, BARD, and Mix—across four distinct logical reasoning categories: Inductive, Abductive, Deductive, and a combined Mix category. The vertical axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0 to 0.8 in increments of 0.2, representing the performance metric. The horizontal plane displays the model names along the front axis and the reasoning categories along the side axis, with each model-category combination represented by a colored 3D bar. Bars are shaded with a gradient from blue (lower accuracy) to yellow (higher accuracy), visually indicating performance levels. For example, Davinci-003 achieves approximately 0.4 accuracy on Inductive, ~0.3 on Abductive, ~0.6 on Deductive, and ~0.7 on Mix; BARD scores ~0.2 on Inductive, ~0.4 on Abductive, ~0.5 on Deductive, and ~0.6 on Mix; and the Mix model performs at ~0.5 on Inductive, ~0.6 on Abductive, ~0.7 on Deductive, and ~0.8 on the Mix category. The chart suggests that performance generally increases from Inductive to Mix reasoning, with the Mix model consistently outperforming the others across all categories. A legend in the lower-left corner identifies Davinci-003 with a gray square, though its corresponding bar is rendered in blue-to-yellow gradient like the others, indicating that the legend may be stylistic rather than color-coded for the bars themselves. The bars are arranged in a grid, with no explicit sorting by height, allowing direct visual comparison across models and reasoning types.
